fun_facts: Growing up in Saint Rose, Louisiana, Justin Jefferson used an empty lot beside his family home to throw a football far and sprint to catch it before it hit the ground.
In LSU’s 2019 season, Justin Jefferson caught 111 passes for 1,540 yards and 18 touchdowns while helping the team reach the College Football Playoff National Championship.
As a rookie, Justin Jefferson had 1,400 receiving yards, setting the post-merger NFL record for a first-year player.
In 2025, Justin Jefferson became the youngest player in NFL history to reach 8,000 receiving yards, at 26 years and 129 days old.

basis.reasoning: ESPN’s biography lists LSU as Justin Jefferson’s college.

The place where [Justin Jefferson](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4262921/justin-jefferson) worked for years to develop into a star receiver at [LSU](https://www.espn.com/college-football/team/_/id/99/lsu-tigers) and first-round draft pick of the [Minnesota Vikings](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/min/minnesota-vikings) is also where his NFL career has begun in earnest.

An empty lot sits adjacent to Jefferson's family home in Saint Rose, Louisiana.

Whenever his parents couldn't find him, it was a safe bet that a young Justin was toiling around the empty lot, heaving a football as far as he could and speeding to catch it before it hit the ground.

excerpts:
offensive-player-of-the-year)

As a rookie, [Justin Jefferson](https://www.nfl.com/players/justin-jefferson/) set the post-merger NFL record for receiving yards by a first-year player with 1,400. In Year 2, he came up 16 yards shy of Randy Moss’ Vikings single-season receiving record of 1,632. And in his third NFL season, Jefferson smashed that mark -- by nearly 200 yards.

Could a 2K season be that far off? What else is he capable of?

Nothing is off the table now for Jefferson, who collected The Associated Press 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year award on Thursday at _NFL Honors_ .
citations.title: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson named AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year | Latest NFL News, Analysis & Updates | NFL.com

excerpts:
[Justin Jefferson](https://www.nfl.com/players/justin-jefferson) ’s milestone moment shouldn’t be lost in the Minnesota Vikings' [dismal outing](https://www.nfl.com/games/vikings-at-chargers-2025-reg-8) Thursday night against the Los Angeles Chargers.

A 15-yard catch late in the second quarter put Jefferson over the 8,000-yard receiving mark for his career, making him the youngest player in NFL history to breach the benchmark.

Jefferson (26 years, 129 days) bested Randy Moss’s previous record by 168 days. He’s just the third player to go for 8,000-plus yards in his first six seasons (Moss, Torry Holt).
